title: Prometheus-alpha v0.6: memory across generations of fission, and attractor basins as a mechanism of robustness
status: Locked before any v0.6 experiment on a confirmatory rule. No new rules, no pilots; a code smoke test at n = 4 on pilot rule S102 checked output shapes only.

H29.claim: Transgenerational memory: split at site 20, the posterior half regrows for 48 steps; repeat three times. The third-generation worm remembers
H29.test: one-sided sign-flip, > 0; Holm over the four rules tested

H30.claim: Attractor basin predicts robustness: across S0, S1, B0, B1, F0, F1, the critical noise sigma* (smallest sigma on the grid 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6 at which Gaussian noise added to the hidden channels of sites 12-19 of decapitated trained bodies halves the regrown head's memory; 64 worms, seed 7030, noise seed 1) is positively rank-correlated with the rule's v0.5 turnover memory (H25)
H30.test: one-sided exact permutation test (720 permutations), alpha 0.05

decision_rules.H29: Holm over F0, F1, S0, S1 at alpha 0.05, SESOI 0.10
decision_rules.H30: p <= 0.05 and rho > 0 (n = 6: low power; a null here is weak evidence)

predictions.H29: F0, F1: supported (each generation repeats the trained split). S0, S1: not supported
